top10.introHtml: The best convertibles across all three sources, ranked by overall value: price vs. mileage, deal ratings, accident history, and driving character. Great Deals and no-accident flags were heavily weighted.

picks.whyGood: Cars.com flagged this BMW 328i Convertible as a Good Deal — the E93 platform is one of the most proven, durable convertibles of its era. At $8,472 with 118K miles, it's priced meaningfully under market for a car with this chassis quality. The BMW 328i convertible is known for its precise steering, balanced chassis, and genuine 4-seat practicality with a powered folding roof.
picks.whatToVerify: Have a BMW-familiar shop inspect the VANOS seals and valve cover gasket (common wear items on the N52). Confirm the folding roof mechanism operates smoothly and all seals are intact. Pull a Carfax and check for rust around the convertible top frame and wheel arches.
picks.bottomLine: Best bang-for-buck entry in the list. If the PPI checks out, a 328i convertible at this price is a smart buy.

picks.whyGood: Only 48,371 miles on a twin-turbo 300hp inline-6 — exceptional for a 2008 model. The 135i is a drivers' car with a rabid enthusiast community and strong aftermarket support. Good Deal badge confirms it's priced below market. The N54 twin-turbo powerplant is one of BMW's most exciting engines of the era.
picks.whatToVerify: The N54 engine is known for injector and high-pressure fuel pump wear — have both inspected. Check the charge pipes for cracks. Confirm the convertible roof electronics work properly. Note: transmission is automatic (not manual as some sources may list).
picks.bottomLine: The lowest-mileage car in this entire search by a wide margin. For a driving enthusiast who wants something special, this is the hidden gem of the list.

picks.whyGood: Newest car in the entire search, with a verified clean title and no-accident history. The 2016 Beetle convertible with the limited-edition Denim package is rare and desirable. VW's 1.8T engine is reliable and well-supported. Private seller with verified clean history is the best combination for a used car.
picks.whatToVerify: Private seller — run a Carfax and have an independent pre-purchase inspection. Verify the convertible roof seals are intact. Check DSG transmission fluid service history if equipped.
picks.bottomLine: The safest bet if you want a modern daily driver with verified clean history. The Denim trim makes it stand out.

picks.whyGood: Great Deal badge plus no-accident history at a franchised INFINITI dealer — 21 miles from Media. The G37 Convertible's 328hp V6 and rear-wheel drive make it one of the most engaging cars in this price range. INFINITI dealers typically do a thorough pre-sale inspection.
picks.whatToVerify: Ask for the dealer inspection report. Check the folding hard-top mechanism carefully — these complex roofs can be expensive to repair. Verify the VQ37VHR engine shows no oil consumption issues.
picks.bottomLine: Great Deal + no accidents + dealer support = strongest combination of value and peace-of-mind in the top 4.

picks.whyGood: A V8 drop-top for under $10K with only 59,000 miles is extraordinary. The E64 645Ci is a grand tourer that commands attention, featuring BMW's N62 4.4L V8 with 325hp and an impeccable interior. Same physical car is listed on AutoTrader (#6) allowing price comparison — CarGurus shows $9,995 vs AutoTrader's $10,884.
picks.whatToVerify: The N62 V8 is known for Vanos actuator wear and valley pan gasket leaks — budget ~$500 for preventive maintenance if not already done. Run a Carfax. This is the same car as #6 — compare both listings and use them as negotiating leverage.
picks.bottomLine: Rare low-mileage V8 at a price that's hard to believe. Worth a thorough PPI — the N62 quirks are well-documented and manageable.

picks.whyGood: No-accident history, only 59K miles, and just 8 miles from Media at a franchised dealer. The same physical car is listed on CarGurus at #5 for $889 less — mention that when negotiating. Audi West Chester is a reputable dealer and will likely have a service history.
picks.whatToVerify: Same N62 V8 concerns as #5. Ask for the full dealer inspection report. Confirm all iDrive electronics, retractable roof, and sensors are operational. Use the CarGurus listing at #5 as negotiating leverage on price.
picks.bottomLine: More practical sibling to #5. With no-accident history and dealer backing, this is the cleaner buy — and the CarGurus listing gives you a $889 price advantage to negotiate with.

picks.whyGood: Clean title + no accidents on a 302hp V8 Mercedes convertible at $7,900 is a remarkable value. The W208 CLK500 is a timeless design and the M113 V8 is one of Mercedes' most reliable engines — well-documented and inexpensive to service compared to more exotic platforms.
picks.whatToVerify: Inspect the hydraulic convertible roof system carefully — these can leak and repairs run $1,000+. Check the air suspension if equipped. Verify the instrument cluster and electronics all function.
picks.bottomLine: Best price per horsepower with verified clean history. The CLK500 looks and feels like a $25K car. Due diligence on the roof seals is the main homework item.

picks.whyGood: Only 8 miles from Media — the closest car in the top 10. The VW Eos is criminally undervalued: its unique glass-panel sunroof integrates with the folding hardtop roof, giving sunroof enjoyment even with the top up. Very practical four-seater with a real trunk. The 2.0T DSG powertrain is smooth and efficient.
picks.whatToVerify: The DSG transmission and the complex roof mechanism are the two things to scrutinize. Have a VW specialist check the roof seals and hydraulic lines. Confirm the DSG fluid has been serviced.
picks.bottomLine: Most practical convertible at this price — real back seat, real trunk, real weather protection. Great for a daily-driver droptop just 8 miles away.

picks.whyGood: Private-seller A5 Cabriolet with Quattro AWD at $8,495 and 80K miles is well under market. The B8 A5 is a sleek, well-engineered convertible with enough luxury to feel premium without the maintenance complexity of the S5 or A8.
picks.whatToVerify: Private sale — Carfax and PPI are essential. The 2.0T timing chain tensioner issue (pre-2012 mostly, but verify) should be confirmed as serviced. Check the folding roof hydraulics and Quattro drivetrain operation.
picks.bottomLine: Solid AWD daily-driver potential at a compelling price. Private sale warrants careful due diligence, but the value here is real.

picks.whyGood: The S5 Cabriolet packs a naturally-aspirated 354hp V8 — a powertrain that Audi later replaced with a less exciting turbocharged V6. This is a future classic. At $9,999 with 92K miles, it's priced fairly for what it is.
picks.whatToVerify: The 4.2L FSI V8 has known carbon buildup issues requiring periodic walnut blasting (~$500). The dual-clutch S-tronic should be fluid-serviced. Confirm the folding roof seals and all quattro drivetrain components.
picks.bottomLine: The connoisseur's pick. A V8 all-wheel-drive convertible under $10K is rare — this won't be this cheap for long.

manual10.introHtml: Manual-transmission convertibles are extremely rare in this market. Across all three sources — Cars.com, CarGurus, and AutoTrader — covering 95+ listings within 35 miles of Media PA, only one genuine manual-transmission convertible was independently verified. CarGurus' manual transmission flag proved unreliable in this search: five cars listed as 'Manual' on CarGurus were verified as automatic when checked directly (including three BMWs and a VW DSG). The sole confirmed manual is a gem worth serious consideration.

picks.whyGood: The only independently verified 6-speed manual-transmission convertible in this entire market search. The 2012 BMW 128i is a pure driver's car — 230hp straight-six, rear-wheel drive, manual gearbox, folding soft-top, and genuine rear seats. Good Deal badge and 86K miles make this a compelling buy for anyone who values the driving experience above all. This car is also cross-listed on Cars.com (ID 97c8159e) for independent price verification.
picks.whatToVerify: Have a BMW specialist inspect the N52 engine VANOS seals and valve cover gasket. Confirm the clutch has reasonable remaining life. Test the folding soft-top through a full open/close cycle. Pull the Carfax — the Cars.com cross-listing can help verify history.
picks.bottomLine: If you've been searching for a genuine manual-transmission open-air car at this price point, this is the needle in the haystack. Act before it's gone.

mustangs.introHtml: Ford Mustang convertibles from 2005 or newer, within 35 miles of Media, PA, priced $7,000–$15,000. The only V8 GT found (2010, 80,750 mi, West Chester, $14,985) is an automatic — all Mustangs in this budget are the 305hp V6, which is a smooth, reliable powertrain. Ranked by overall value, with the best no-accident verified listings at top.

picks.whyGood: No-accident history is the standout on this listing — AutoTrader verified clean accident record at Josie's Auto Sales, a known Gilbertsville dealer. 305hp V6 automatic is a smooth, reliable powertrain. This same car is listed on CarGurus at $9,900 (see #4) — compare both and use the lower price for negotiation.
picks.whatToVerify: Confirm the convertible top seal condition. Ask for the dealer inspection report. Check transmission fluid and service history.
picks.bottomLine: Best combination of no-accident history and fair pricing among the Mustangs. The CarGurus cross-listing gives you price leverage.

picks.whyGood: Cars.com issued a Great Deal badge — this is priced below comparable listings. Langhorne PA is local, and Discount Auto is a known dealer. The Great Deal flag provides market validation that the ask is competitive.
picks.whatToVerify: No accident/title data from Cars.com — run a Carfax. Confirm convertible top condition and inspect the 3.7L V6 for maintenance history.
picks.bottomLine: Great Deal badge makes this worth a first call. Local Langhorne dealer at a competitive price.

picks.whyGood: Lowest mileage of the automatic V6 Mustangs in this search at 109,452 miles — a meaningful longevity advantage. Clayton NJ is within range. This car is also cross-listed on CarGurus and AutoTrader — check all three listings before visiting.
picks.whatToVerify: No accident history data available from this source — run a Carfax. Fair Deal suggests it's priced at market. PPI recommended.
picks.bottomLine: Best mileage of the group at a fair price. The 109K miles vs 121K–128K on the others is worth the modest premium.

picks.whyGood: Cheapest Mustang in the search at $9,900 — same physical car as #1 (Josie's Auto Sales Gilbertsville) but CarGurus often shows a lower price than AutoTrader for the same listing. Use this CarGurus price as leverage when dealing with the AT listing at $10,390.
picks.whatToVerify: Same car as the AT listing at #1 — verify the actual transaction price directly with Josie's. Inspect top, transmission fluid, and suspension.
picks.bottomLine: If the dealer will honor the CarGurus price, this is the best-value Mustang in the search with 121K miles and no-accident history on the AT listing.

picks.whyGood: No-accident history verified by AutoTrader — same mileage bracket as the Langhorne car at #2 but independently sourced with clean accident record. 34 miles from Media is the furthest but within the search radius.
picks.whatToVerify: No dealer information available — verify seller type (private or dealer). Carfax and standard PPI apply.
picks.bottomLine: Backup option with no-accident history. If top picks fall through, this is a solid alternative.
